_meta.indication: ISENTRESS (raltegravir), an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor, indicated in combination with other antiretroviral agents for treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-experienced adult patients who have evidence of viral replication and HIV-1 strains resistant to multiple antiretroviral agents.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 018 (Phase III, Europe, Asia, Central and South America)
pivotal_trials.design: Phase III multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of raltegravir 400 mg bid plus OBT vs OBT alone; 2:1 randomization
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-experienced HIV-infected patients who had failed prior antiretroviral therapy (triple-class resistant)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving HIV RNA < 400 copies/mL at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: 178/228 (78.1%) of subjects in Study 018 had HIV RNA < 400 copies/mL at Week 16; placebo 41% in study 018

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 019 (Phase III, North, Central and South America)
pivotal_trials.design: Phase III multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of raltegravir plus OBT vs OBT alone (identical design to Study 018, different geographic region)
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-experienced HIV-infected patients who had failed prior antiretroviral therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients achieving HIV RNA < 400 copies/mL at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: 177/226 (78.3%) of patients in Study 019 had HIV RNA < 400 copies/mL at Week 16; placebo 43% in study 019

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (treatment-experienced, studies 005/018/019): diarrhea (16.6% vs 19.5% OBT), nausea (9.9% vs 14.2%), headache (9.7% vs 11.7%), pyrexia (4.9% vs 10.3%). Events more frequent on raltegravir: fatigue (7.9% vs 4.6%), nasopharyngitis (6.1% vs 3.9%), rash (5.3% vs 2.5%), herpes zoster (4.1% vs 0.7%). CK elevation in ~6.6% raltegravir vs 4.1% controls.
target_moa: Raltegravir inhibits the catalytic activity of HIV-1 integrase (strand transfer), preventing integration of HIV-1 DNA into the host cell genome and thereby blocking formation of the HIV-1 provirus required for propagation of viral infection.

advisory_committee.vote: Presented at the Antiviral Products Advisory Committee on September 5, 2007; the committee unanimously recommended approval.

summary.text: NDA 22-145 for raltegravir, an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor, received a priority review for an unmet medical need and was approved under accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.510) based on plasma HIV-1 RNA response through 24 weeks in two controlled trials in treatment-experienced adults; the Antiviral Products Advisory Committee unanimously recommended approval, and confirmatory Week 48 data from Studies 018 and 019 were required post-marketing.

requirement.text: Deferred pediatric study (PREA) for HIV-1 infection in subjects 2 to 18 years of age, determining PK (pharmacokinetic profile) followed by 24 weeks of dosing; final study report by June 30, 2011.

citations.quote: 2. Deferred pediatric study under PREA for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in pediatric subjects from 2 to 18 years of age. This study will determine raltegravir exposure (pharmacokinetic profile) followed by 24 weeks of dosing. Efficacy will be based on viral load reduction through 24 weeks of dosing and safety will be monitored for a minimum of 24 weeks to support raltegravir dose selection, safety, and efficacy in this population.
